attributes.body_ja:
「かけ」は、「向（む）け」と同（おな）じように造語（ぞうご）とされている言葉（ことば）です。動詞（どうし）の「掛（か）ける」からできています。これは動詞（どうし）の連用形（れんようけい）につながって、「(A) を途中（とちゅう）までしているが、まだ完全（かんぜん）には終（お）わっていない」や「(A) が今（いま）にも起（お）こりそう」という意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）します。

「かけ」は、名詞（めいし）のように働（はたら）きます。そのため、別（べつ）の名詞（めいし）に付（つ）くときは格助詞（かくじょし）の「の」が必要（ひつよう）です。また、文（ぶん）の終（お）わりで使（つか）われるときは「だ」が必要（ひつよう）です。

名詞形（めいしけい）の「かけ」ではなく、動詞（どうし）の「掛（か）ける」がそのまま使（つか）われることもあります。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「掛（か）ける」には、「（何（なに）かで支（ささ）えながら）高（たか）いところにぶら下（さ）げる」というような意味（いみ）があります。この何（なに）かが始（はじ）まりにも終（お）わりにもつかず、その過程（かてい）の中（なか）で、引（ひ）っかかって浮（う）かんでいるイメージが、「物事（ものごと）が確定（かくてい）していない・終（お）わっていない」というニュアンスにつながっている、と考（かんが）えられるでしょう。

「かけ」につながる動詞（どうし）が瞬間動詞（しゅんかんどうし）の場合（ばあい）、「かけ」は「今（いま）にも起（お）こりそうだ」という意味（いみ）になります。

一方（いっぽう）で、継続動詞（けいぞくどうし）の場合（ばあい）、「かけ」は「(A) をしている途中（とちゅう）」という意味（いみ）になります。
attributes.body:
Being an unofficial helper verb, かけ is what is known as a 造語（ぞうご） (neologism), and carries one specific meaning when used in conjunction with other words. This is similar to 向（む）け. かけ comes from the verb 掛（か）ける 'to suspend', and may be attached to the conjunctive form of other verbs, in order to convey that they are 'unfinished'. Usually this translates as 'half (A)', 'about to (A)', or 'not yet finished (A)'.

かけ behaves like a noun, so may be followed by the case marking particle の when attached directly to another noun, or by だ when at the end of a sentence.

Occasionally, the verb 掛（か）ける itself may be used instead of the noun form, かけ.

Fun Fact

As the literal meaning of 掛（か）ける is 'to suspend', it expresses that something is stuck somewhere in the process of happening. This is similar to taking a photo of someone that is jumping. In the photo it will look like they are 'suspended', but that is only because one particular moment has been captured, somewhere between the start and the finish. かけ conveys exactly the same meaning, and therefore may be interpreted differently, depending on the verb it is paired with.

With verbs that express a momentary action (something that cannot be 'half' done), かけ will convey that the action was 'on the verge of' happening.

However, with verbs that are ongoing actions, かけ will simply imply that they are 'in the process' of being done.

attributes.body: ところだ and かけ both express incomplete actions, but with a key difference. るところだ emphasizes that the action is just about to happen, e.g. リンゴを食べるところだ ('I'm about to eat an apple.'). かけ indicates the action has started but isn't finished, e.g. 食べかけのリンゴ ('a half-eaten apple').

attributes.body: Both かけ and たて describe transitional states of actions, but with opposite timing. かけ refers to something that is incomplete or in progress, often implying interrupted action, e.g. 食べかけのパン 'half-eaten bread'. たて, by contrast, refers to something freshly completed, emphasizing newness and immediacy, e.g. 焼きたてのパン 'freshly baked bread'.

attributes.body: はじめる attaches to verb stems to mean 'to begin' or 'start' doing something, e.g. 食べはじめる 'to start eating'. In contrast, かけ also attaches to verb stems but indicates something incomplete or in progress, e.g. 食べかけ 'half-eaten'. Forms with かけ function grammatically as nouns, as in 食べかけのバナナ 'a half-eaten banana'.

attributes.body: かけ and だす both attach to verb stems and can express the start of an action, but their nuance differs. かけ emphasizes that the action has begun but remains incomplete. For example, 書きかけの小説 'a partially written/incomplete novel.' In contrast, だす highlights the beginning of the action, often with a sense of suddenness. For example, 書き出した ('He suddenly started writing.').
